correctness.rationale: All finite type-A cases follow by the full proof: idempotent parabolic classification, connected-union commutation criterion via Bruhat-downward-closed proper-parabolic-product contradiction, unique omitted root in a maximal clique, recursive Cartesian factorization and BST ideal bijection. Direct 0-Hecke multiplication independently verified all maximal cliques through m=7, and all monoid idempotents through m=5.

evidence: Elias–Ko 2021, Lemmas 2.2 and 2.9 provide the structural ingredients, not maximal-family classification.
He 2009, Section 1, constructs a commutative submonoid not identified with the full set of maximal commuting idempotent families.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general Coxeter or semigroup classification could imply the present path-graph theorem, but this stronger coverage was not located in the inspected primary texts. The proved result is confined to type A; a priori generalizations are not asserted.

evidence: Elias–Ko 2021 gives an idempotent classification and Demazure containment but not the clique classification.
He 2009 concerns a different commutative construction.
Ganyushkin–Mazorchuk 2010 counts quotient elements, not commuting-family cliques.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior classification of the vertices and multiplication is logically weaker than the new exhaustive classification of maximal compatible vertex families; the proof supplies a nontrivial Bruhat obstruction and recursive unique-root lemma. Algebra-idempotent commutation and quotient monoid cardinalities do not imply the maximal-clique cardinality spectrum. A hypothetical unlocated nested-set characterization is a residual coverage risk.

evidence: Elias–Ko 2021, Lemma 2.9: idempotents correspond to longest parabolic elements.
Denton 2011, Chapter 2: distinct notion of orthogonal idempotents in a monoid algebra.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalent formulations include maximal cliques of the monoid-idempotent commutation graph and maximal compatible parabolic supports. The algebra-idempotent literature and the Catalan quotient-monoid construction concern different objects. No equivalent all-maximal-cliques/tree statement was found in the materially examined sources.

evidence: Ganyushkin–Mazorchuk 2010, Theorem 1(vi–viii) counts elements of a quotient monoid by Catalan numbers.
The independently calculated \(m=4\) maximal-clique size spectrum is \(8\) of size \(5\), \(2\) of size \(6\), and \(4\) of size \(7\).
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The matching Catalan total in quotient-monoid tables is not the number of maximal commuting families in this graph and does not determine their size spectrum. No exact database/tabulated spectrum for the present invariant was located; this is not claimed to establish priority.

originality.rationale: The primary 2021 Elias–Ko paper proves the vertex/idempotent classification and Demazure coset containment but not the maximal compatible family or size spectrum. He, Denton, and Ganyushkin–Mazorchuk study logically different commutative constructions, algebra idempotents, and quotient monoid cardinality respectively. Exact-claim searches and available publication comparisons showed no prior implication; residual risk of an unlocated general Coxeter/nested-set statement is recorded.
residual_risks: An as-yet unlocated theorem on Coxeter parabolic commuting idempotents or graph-associahedron nested sets may subsume this classification.
The literature search does not establish independent publication priority.

value.rationale: Canonical monoid idempotents have a natural commuting graph whose maximal cliques represent maximal commuting semilattices. Every such family has a unique binary-tree structure; the Catalan census and complete nonuniform clique-size spectrum solve intrinsic structural invariants of an infinite family, beyond the known 2^m vertex enumeration.
